change.authority_owner: GAS/movement unchanged; new timer is cosmetic animation-worker state

analysis.steady_window: All raw samples with elapsed_seconds > 0.7; settle uses its entire separate capture.
analysis.yaw_delta: Shortest signed degrees in [-180,180); counts use 0.0001 degree zero threshold. Reversal-pattern negative steps are intentional.
analysis.bone_step: Angular distance 2*acos(abs(dot(normalized quaternion pairs))) in degrees, consecutive published component-space bone rotations.
analysis.correlation: Pearson correlation of bone angular step and absolute leg-alpha change from the same adjacent sample pair; null means effectively constant series.
analysis.rates: Angular total variation / observed capture-window seconds; sample cadence is adjacent sample count / window seconds.
analysis.final_tuning_reported_by_author: 5 deg/s enter, 2 deg/s exit, 150 ms grace. This report analyzes outcomes; it does not independently export asset tuning.

limitations: Slate snapshots are not NetworkPrediction simulation frames; this analysis does not claim finalized NP sync-state sampling.
Published AnimInstance fields and bone poses may have different evaluation phases. No animation evaluation was forced.
Input action injection exercises the configured input path, not physical device mapping/modifier behavior.
The same mouse magnitude is injected once per callback, so differing sample rates change achieved yaw speed. Inputs match by action/mode/magnitude, not exact camera trajectory or animation phase.

Capture rates differ across runs, approximately 56-63 samples/s; measurement overhead is present and unquantified. Per-sample steps, travel per second and actual yaw rate are all retained rather than claiming perfectly equal-speed A/B.
Bone rotation metrics measure observed pose changes, not a universal visual-quality threshold. Residual legitimate locomotion/IK changes remain; no exact source/target pose parity is asserted.
The slow-stick before-02 run is retained as a nonmatching low-turn-rate diagnostic, not substituted for a matching mouse baseline.
Quiet-return timing is relative to a separately started capture and does not directly measure the configured 150 ms grace from the final input event.
CMC is represented only by final-state measurements; there is no measured CMC before/after improvement claim.
